# requireSymbol

<link-summary>Returns the value as a symbol, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireSymbol() — Returns the value as a symbol, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireSymbol(value: unknown, message: string = "Expected a symbol."): symbol;
```

Registered symbols from `Symbol.for` and the well-known symbols both pass; nothing else does.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                       | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :---------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                         | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a symbol."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`symbol` — the same value, typed as a symbol.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                  |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a symbol. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireSymbol(Symbol("id")); // => Symbol("id")
requireSymbol(Symbol.iterator); // => Symbol.iterator
requireSymbol("id"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireSymbol(null); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
